title: FRNet: Frequency-based Rotation Network for Long-term Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Long-term time series forecasting must predict future values over long horizons while modeling complex and important period behavior.

gap.claim: Existing studies mainly model static periods with fixed time steps and rarely capture dynamic periods in the time domain.

contributions.claim: FRNet explores dynamic period features through rotation in the frequency domain.
FRNet decomposes time series into period and trend components and uses complex-valued linear networks with separate frequency rotation modules to predict them.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe FRNet as a novel long-term time series forecasting method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on seven real-world datasets.
The authors report that FRNet consistently outperforms various state-of-the-art methods.
The source code is reported as publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-term forecasting predicts future values from historical time series, with period behavior as an essential component.
Prior work has limitations in modeling dynamic complicated periods and generally focuses on static periods.
The authors report that period changes are more readily captured and quantified in the frequency domain.
FRNet applies frequency-domain rotation to dynamic period features, decomposing the series and predicting period and trend components with separate rotation modules.
Experiments on seven real-world datasets are reported to show superiority over various state-of-the-art methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, baselines, dataset names, or experimental settings.
